Pete Fiutak · College Football News Fri, November 20, 2026 at 8:22 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For two 5-5 teams, Iowa State and UCF have certainly played fascinating seasons. Iowa State gave Iowa everything it could handle in a 16-13 Hawkeye win, played well in a loss to Utah, won wild firefights against West Virginia and Oklahoma State, and, in a stunner, blew away Cincinnati 41-13 last week. For a rebuilding year, this has been a blast. UCF was the team that beat BYU right after the giant Cougar win over Notre Dame. It's been up and down, though, with some puzzling clunkers to go along with the five wins. Get this, though, and there's a shot at the program's first winning season since 2022. Iowa State vs UCF: Quick Hits Iowa State gets Kansas State at home next week for a shot at a sixth win if it doesn't happen Friday night. UCF needs to win this with a dangerous date at Colorado to close the regular season. It's the second meeting between the two teams. Iowa State won 38-35 in 2024. How To Watch Iowa State vs UCF Date: Friday, November 20, 2026 Game Time: 6:00 PM ET TV: FS1 Location: Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando, FL – Week 12 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 25 – CFN Week 12 Expert Picks Why Iowa State Will Win UCF is miserable on third downs. It can't convert them, can't stop them, and it's a huge problem for a team that's so maddeningly inconsistent. Iowa State is just as bad offensively at keeping the chains moving, but it's great at holding up against teams that can't run the ball effectively enough. Don't run, don't get easy third down chances, and it all rolls from there. If the Cyclones win this, though, it'll be on the other side of the ball. UCF has a rough time against decent passers, and Iowa State's Jaylen Raynor got hot at the right time, throwing for over 800 yards with six touchdown over his last three games. Why UCF Will Win Iowa State doesn't win on the road. It doesn't turn the ball over, and there isn't a penalty problem. The issue has been the opponents – the Cyclones had to deal with Iowa, BYU, and Arizona – but the defense didn't hold up against Baylor, either. Everything focuses around Aiden Flora, the nation's leading rusher with 1,335 yards and 12 scores. When he's rumbling, Iowa State wins. Against FBS teams, Iowa State is 4-0 when Flora runs for 190 yards or more, and is 0-5 when he doesn't. UCF's issue is the pass defense. The run defense has held up well, allowing just 3.6 yards per carry. Iowa State vs UCF Prediction, Betting Lines Which UCF team will run out of the tunnel? When things are clicking, the Knights can hang with anyone – like they showed against BYU. But when the defense isn't taking the ball away and the offense isn't finding its up-tempo groove, forget it. Iowa State has only turned the ball over more than once in one game: the loss to Utah. It won't give the ball up, and the offensive balance will be there to finally get the first road win of the year. Quick slant: This game marks the second meeting between the two schools, with Iowa State leading the series 1-0. In that 2024 game, running back RJ Harvey (196 yards) and quarterback Jacurri Brown (154) rushed for over 150 yards and two touchdowns apiece to spark UCF, but Cyclones quarterback Rocco Becht scored both the go-ahead touchdown and subsequent two-point conversion with 30 seconds left to lift ISU to a 38-35 win in Ames. Iowa State is making its second trip to Orlando after defeating then-No. 15 Miami in the 2024 Pop-Tarts Bowl at Camping World Stadium. A win on Friday would make UCF bowl-eligible for the first time since 2023. About UCF (5-5, 3-4 Big 12): Receiver Josh Derry leads UCF in receptions (52), receiving yards (702) and receiving touchdowns (4). The senior transfer has back-to-back 100-yard receiving games and could become the first Knight since Kobe Hudson in 2023 with three straight 100-yard performances. Tight end Caden Piening is tied for the nation's lead in touchdowns among rookie tight ends with three. He is tied with Wake Forest's Dominick Barry and Hawaii's Frank Abreu. About Iowa State (5-5, 3-4 Big 12): Iowa State is winless on the road (0-4) this season and is 13-10 in its last 23 games away from Jack Trice Stadium. The Cyclones are trying to become bowl-eligible for the ninth time in the last 11 seasons. Linebacker Sullivan Schlimgen is third in the Big 12 with 93 tackles. Kicker Kyle Konrardy holds the school record with seven 50-plus-yard kicks in his career, including two this season, highlighted by a 57-yarder in a 42-31 loss to Baylor on Nov. 7. Three things to watch 1. Iowa State leads the Big 12 and is third in the nation in red zone offense, with the Cyclones scoring on 29 of 30 attempts inside the opponent's 20-yard line. ISU's perfect streak was snapped when it failed to score in the red zone in last week's 41-13 win over Cincinnati. 2. UCF is 4-0 this season when scoring 30-plus points in a game and 24-1 overall under Frost, but is just 1-5 when scoring 30 points or less this season. Iowa State has allowed an opponent to score 30-plus points five times this season, all against Big 12 opposition. 3. UCF quarterback Alonza Barnett III has thrown at least one touchdown in his previous eight career starts and in 12 of his past 13 starts, going back to last season.

away.blurb: UCF Senior Ruled Out For Senior Knight vs. Iowa State: Injury Report Breakdown Skip to main content SI.COM In addition to only one defensive back being ruled out in UCF's Tuesday player availability report, the Knights are trending toward getting back their leading rusher against the Cyclones. The Knights are trending toward relief in the secondary, with both DJ Bell and Kahmel Johnson ruled probable in Tuesday's report. However, the unit won't be fully all-hands-on-deck, as Demari Henderson was ruled out . As for Bell, a senior, and Johnson, they are set to return to their rotational roles, barring any setbacks. Bell, after missing four games, would be back rotating with Jayden Bellamy and Antione Jackson . Johnson, after missing two games, would return as the backup nickelback behind Braeden Marshall . Three Knights were ruled questionable in Tuesday's report. UCF's coach said the senior was a game-time decision before the Oct. 30 matchup against the Baylor Bears, and if not, he'd be a game-time decision on the road against the Kansas Jayhawks. UCF LB Lewis Carter Reflects on Recovering From Injury - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF 'GTA 6' impacts sports UCF LB Lewis Carter Reflects on Recovering From Injury (Mike Watters/Imagn Images) Demetrius Montero · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 18, 2026 at 12:36 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Lewis Carter missed six straight conference games before returning in the UCF Knights ' 26-13 loss to the Arizona State Sun Devils last Saturday. Carter sustained a knee injury in Week 3 against the Georgia State Panthers, as fans and media saw him enter the medical tent. Coach Scott Frost said he was unaware his senior was injured, and it spiraled into missing the star linebacker. Their captain made his conference debut against Arizona State. He had a quiet performance, posting three solo tackles. The star linebacker said he's 100% and wants to put his best foot forward to help his team win. UCF is one win away from a bowl game, snapping a two-year drought. Carter quarterbacks the defense, communicates adjustments when the offense audibles and shores up tackling. He led the team with 92 tackles last season and was on pace to continue wearing the crown until he got injured. UCF sorely missed his presence over the middle, but its depth stepped up. Tackett Curtis is the team's leading tackler with a career-high 67 tackles, two passes defended, two sacks and two interceptions. Jahleel Culbreath and Jayden Jennings have contributed alongside Curtis. They tallied 67 tackles, three pass deflections and 1.5 sacks. The Knights' front seven got its best linebacker back during a crucial Friday game against the Cyclones. Frost said they will be a " good challenge " with a dual-threat quarterback and the Big 12's leading rusher. Aiden Flora leads with 1,335 yards and is second with 12 touchdowns. Flora has tallied five 150-plus-yard games and four multi-touchdown games. He rushed for a career-high 221 yards in a 51-49 upset over the then-No. 24 Oklahoma State Cowboys and reached a career-best three touchdowns twice: once in a 45-42 win over the West Virginia Mountaineers and in a 41-13 blowout over the Cincinnati Bearcats. Carter's ability to blow up the run game is what UCF needs to avenge last week's disappointing loss and send him off with one final home win

home.blurb: “Lewis, like a lot of our guys, he's been out a long time,” said coach Scott Frost . “He’s going to continue to get better as he gets closer to 100% and shakes the rust off a little bit. He’s a great person and a great player. He’s one of our leaders and we’ve missed him.” Ex-UCF star Tacko Fall, now with 76ers, says time was right for NBA return Florida & Caribbean Experiences Branded Content Paid Partner Content Services About the Orlando Sentinel 🎁 Gift idea: Sentinel's 150th book Flooding hits Central Florida as rain continues to dump buckets across region This was supposed to be Lewis Carter ‘s breakout season. Instead, the UCF linebacker and team captain found himself on the sideline with an injury that cost him half the season. Carter, 22, returned against Arizona State on Saturday, playing for the first time since Sept. 19 against Georgia State. “I was flying around and had a lot of energy. It felt good,” said Carter, who finished with three tackles on 25 snaps. In Carter’s absence, transfer Tackett Curtis has emerged as the team’s leading tackler (67), along with Jahleel Culbreath (44), Jaden Jennings (23), and Cole Kozlowski (19), who returned after a court order in fall camp. Carter spent much of his time off the field mentoring his teammates. “I was being hands-on as much as I could within the meeting rooms and on the sidelines,” said Carter. “I was trying to be a voice for the guys throughout.” How important are turnovers against Iowa State? Iowa State has turned the ball over just nine times — tied for the second-fewest turnovers given up in the Big 12 this season. Meanwhile, UCF has struggled to create takeaways lately, failing to force a turnover for the second time in its last three games. The Knights are 1-9 under Frost when they don’t force a miscue, including an 0-3 mark this season. “At times, we’ve been really good and the games where we’ve gotten turnovers, we’ve won those games,” said Frost. “That’s no secret. That’s the biggest stat in football.” Frost credits the takeaways with not only giving the team much-needed momentum, but also shortening the field and giving the offense more chances to score. Something the Knights could use more of over the remaining two games. How can the Knights get more pressure on the quarterback? UCF has gone back-to-back games without sacking a quarterback for the first time since 2021. The Knights have 16 sacks heading into this week’s showdown, tied for the second-fewest in the Big 12 with Iowa State. “We’ve actually gotten a lot of pressure, but we haven’t gotten the sacks,” said Frost. “As far as affecting throws, our guys have been pretty good. picks.blurb: Nebraska Football vs. Ohio State Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Can Nebraska finally beat a ranked team under Matt Rhule? The Huskers get their shot against Ohio State in Lincoln on Senior Day. It’s the last home game of the year, and a win would change how a lot of fans feel about this season. On the Carriker Chronicles, Adam Carriker breaks down why Nebraska has a chance, what worries him most, and why he thinks this game could still be up for grabs in the fourth quarter. Nebraska’s shutout of Rutgers showed how good this defense can be. The running game also put together a complete performance, which gives the Huskers something to build on. But can they run the ball against Ohio State when the Buckeyes know it’s coming? Carriker wants Nebraska to run with a purpose and give Anthony Colandrea some quick answers in the passing game. Get the tight ends involved. Take a few shots downfield when the matchup is there. And when it’s third down, give Ohio State something it hasn’t already seen. At some point, somebody has to win a one-on-one matchup. The biggest question on defense is Jeremiah Smith. How does Rob Aurich keep a receiver that good from taking over the game? That job gets tougher with Andrew Marshall out. Carriker talks through how Nebraska can mix up its pressure and make Ohio State work for its yards. A couple of big plays can undo an otherwise good afternoon for the defense. The Huskers need to keep Smith from getting loose and give themselves a chance to get off the field on third down. Carriker also spends time on something that could decide a close game: where each team starts with the ball. Archie Wilson can help Nebraska by pinning Ohio State deep and making the Buckeyes drive the length of the field. A turnover could give the Huskers a short field, but Nebraska has to cash in when it gets to the red zone. And if the defense or special teams can put seven points on the board themselves, that changes what the offense has to do to win. Carriker’s four keys are to win in the margins, limit what Ohio State does best, win the fourth quarter, and score a touchdown on defense or special teams. He sees a real path to an upset with the way Nebraska’s defense has played, the progress in the run game, and a home crowd that wants to send the seniors out with a win. In the end, the Huskers have yet to show us they can put together four full quarters against a team as good as Ohio State and the Jeremiah Smith matchup and Marshall’s absence are hard for him to get past. The 7-3 Buckeyes climbed six spots to No. 14 in Tuesday’s playoff rankings , just outside the top 12. McElroy didn’t spare the Buckeyes’ front either. “The offensive line just doesn’t move anybody off the ball,” he said, adding that Ohio State averages 4.1 yards per carry. That puts more of the load on Jeremiah Smith, the Heisman Trophy betting favorite with 1,317 receiving yards and 15 touchdowns. However, McElroy warned that a pass-heavy game plan is a bad sign for Ohio State. “When Ryan Day’s team throws it 40 or more times, he’s just 5-5,” he said. Can Nebraska pull the upset? Defensive tackle Jahsear Whittington, who leads the team with six sacks, left the Rutgers win with an apparent knee injury. “One of the main things from that game to take away is just the amount of guys that stepped up with injuries ,” Rhule said. Nebraska’s kicking is another worry, since the Huskers are 6 of 13 on field goals. McElroy said that when a drive stalls, “it’s a coin flip on whether or not they walk out with points.” McElroy picks Ohio State to win 19-17. “I do, however, think that Nebraska will make a mistake or two, which ultimately gives Ohio State the victory,” he said. The Buckeyes looked unprepared, sloppy, and undisciplined en route to a 30-18 loss in L.A., and followed that up with an u ninspiring beatdown at the hands of Oregon in Columbus to the tune of 41-28. However, the Buckeyes bounced back last week and took down Northwestern 28-19 to get back on track. Next up is a road trip to Nebraska before things close out at home vs. -- ahem, you know -- Michigan . And now, thanks to the latest College Football Playoff rankings, it sure feels like Ohio State is in the mix to get into the playoff if it wins out and gets a little help. In fact, Ohio State checked in at No. 14 in the third release of the rankings just released on Tuesday, and that's six spots higher already than the week prior and just three spots away from making the 12-team field. According to the analytics ESPN uses to predict the chances of victory, Ohio State has a 71.3% chance of beating the Cornhuskers . That's good and fine, but we have to remember that this same model had the Buckeyes with a significant chance of beating the Trojans on the road, and then the Ducks at home, and neither of those turned out so well. Hopefully, the worldwide leader has this one right just like last week, and we can be celebrating a much-needed win to set up a matchup against Michigan that could be bigger than we thought just a couple of weeks ago. Since these analytics are updated by game results only, there's no chance of this percentage changing, but the Buckeyes will still need to execute at a high level, help out freshman quarterback Luke Fahey , and not make as many mental mistakes, especially on the road. The game is set to kick off at Noon ET on Fox, and we'll have more on the game leading up to Saturday, and be around during and after as well for extensive coverage. Hopefully, we are setting the stage for "The Game" with some things on the line. (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images thehooch36 · SB Nation Tue, November 17, 2026 at 5:22 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Well, would you look at that? Nebraska just shut out a Big Ten opponent on the road. The Huskers dispatched Rutgers 31–0 on Saturday, and while the Scarlet Knights aren't exactly setting the college football world on fire, shutting out a conference opponent is no small accomplishment. Now comes Ohio State. COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 14: Ohio State mascot Brutus joins the Ohio State Buckeyes in the singing of "Carmen Ohio" following a 28-19 victory over the Northwestern Wildcats at Ohio Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Normally, that name alone would be enough to make Nebraska fans start calculating how much bourbon they'll need by halftime. But these aren't the same Buckeyes we've grown accustomed to seeing. Ohio State has three losses. Three! In Columbus, that's practically grounds for declaring a state of emergency. And according to Ramsey from Eleven Warriors, who joined Monday Night Therapy this week, the problems aren't imaginary. The offensive line has struggled. The tight ends apparently believe blocking is an optional extracurricular activity. Special teams have been an adventure, and not the enjoyable kind. The Buckeyes are also starting true freshman quarterback Luke Fahey, who's talented but still learning on the job. Those are a lot of vulnerabilities for a program accustomed to simply reloading every season. Of course, Ohio State still has Jeremiah Smith. COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 14: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes runs with the ball as Damon Walters #21 of the Northwestern Wildcats defends during the fourth quarter of a game at Ohio Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) | Getty Images And therein lies the problem. Smith might be the best receiver in college football. Nebraska can scheme, disguise coverages, and pressure the quarterback all afternoon, but Smith is capable of making one play that changes everything. So how does Nebraska keep him from doing that? Run. The. Damn. Ball. Control possession. Move the chains. Keep the clock running. Make Ohio State's offense spend as much time watching from the sideline as possible. And when it's third-and-two, perhaps we could actually gain two yards instead of getting unnecessarily creative. Just a thought. Nebraska's defense has momentum after its performance against Rutgers, and a home crowd in Lincoln should make life uncomfortable for a freshman quarterback. The opportunity is there. But opportunity and execution haven't always been particularly close friends in Lincoln. Nebraska vs. Ohio State Betting Odds The betting discussion has centered on Ohio State as a narrow favorite. The FanDuel Sportsbook currently has the visitors as a 3.5-point favorite. The over/under is currently 41.5 points. Personally, I think Ohio State would deserve to be favored by six or seven points on a neutral field. But Memorial Stadium isn't neutral, and this isn't an Ohio State team without weaknesses. The Buckeyes have the talent to win this game. Nebraska has the opportunity to make that talent irrelevant for long stretches. Whether the Huskers can actually pull that off is another question entirely. Choose wisely. Play responsibly. And Go Big Red. Always.

home.blurb: Defensive back Andrew Marshall is out , as Matt Rhule announced earlier this week that one of the nation's top cornerbacks will miss the rest of Nebraska’s season. The good news for the Huskers is that defensive lineman Anthony Jones Jr. was upgraded from “out” last week to “questionable” this week. With this being the first injury report of the week, there’s now hope that he could be upgraded to probable by Friday and then suit up on Saturday morning. For Ohio State, the guys who are out were all expected to be out. Quarterback Julian Sayin, running back Ja'Kobi Jackson, safety Deshawn Stewart, wide receiver Brennen Schramm, offensive linemen Jaxon Powell and Max Riley, and tight end Maxence LeBlanc will miss the game against the Cornhuskers. The biggest piece of positive news for the Buckeyes is that senior left guard Luke Montgomery is expected to return. Montgomery is ready to roll after not appearing on the report, while both Daniels and Boyd are listed as questionable. Montgomery and Daniels had flu-like symptoms last week, while Boyd has been battling a sprained ankle for more than a month. No surprises popped up on the availability report for Ohio State, unlike last week when Montgomery was initially listed as questionable. That suggests the Buckeyes avoided any major new injuries in their win over Northwestern. Of course, the biggest absence of all for OSU is quarterback Julian Sayin. That might not be as big a problem for Ryan Day and company after his replacement, Luke Fahey , finally had a very solid outing. Against Northwestern, Fahey completed 21 of 32 passes for 201 yards and 3 touchdowns. He also threw an interception, but the biggest step forward was that he seemed to figure out a secret to the offense: Just get the ball to Jeremiah Smith. Without Owen Chambliss, Jahsear Whittington, and Andrew Marshall, Nebraska will have its work cut out for it on Saturday morning. home.headline: Andrew Marshall injury could keep Nebraska from taking the next step in evolution
home.blurb: Marshall missed the Huskers’ game against Rutgers this past weekend, and on Monday, head coach Matt Rhule confirmed that the star defensive back is out for the rest of the season. When Nebraska faces off against Ohio State on Saturday, the Huskers know they won’t have to face quarterback Julian Sayin . However, they’ll still have to face all-time great wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, which is why losing Andrew Marshall is a big blow. Rhule said that Marshall suffered a stress fracture in his leg against Illinois but continued to play after suffering the injury. Since that game, Marshall has undergone surgery to repair the fracture and has played his last down for Nebraska in his college football career. Marshall finished the 2026 season with 28 tackles, an interception, and a team-high six pass breakups. He’s long been considered one of the best defensive backs in the country, and Rhule made that point when addressing the injury. Andrew Marshall season-ending injury leaves Nebraska football without shutdown corner vs. Ohio State “I think he’s as good as there is in the country and I think everyone knows it,” Rhule said during his Monday press conference. “I think everyone’s seen it.” The California native is one of NU’s best transfer-portal stories after arriving from Idaho before the 2025 campaign. Nebraska routinely lined him up opposite an opponent’s best receiver and often left him in one-on-one coverage while devoting defensive help elsewhere. Marshall was targeted just 44 times this season and allowed just 15 receptions for 237 yards. 93 of those yards came against Illinois, as it was easily his worst game of the season. Playing on a bum leg certainly explains why he struggled against Illinois’ Colin Dixon, who was recently named to the latest Fred Biletnikoff Award watch list. Nebraska started Victor Evans and freshman Danny Odem at cornerback against Rutgers and will move forward with the same duo along with Jeremiah Charles. Junior Larry Tarver is also set to see more rotational action. Without Nebraska’s shutdown corner, beating Ohio State became even tougher on Monday. It’s unlikely that one corner will be assigned to Smith the way defensive coordinator Rob Aurich might have assigned Marshall if he were healthy. Nebraska is obviously hoping that a change in offensive coordinator and the end of the four-game losing streak will allow the Huskers to finish the season strong. Beating Ohio State in Lincoln is never easy, but this version of the Buckeyes has shown they are flawed. picks.headline: 3 Bold Predictions for Wisconsin vs. Purdue: Don't Count out Colton Joseph Just Yet
picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for Wisconsin vs. Purdue: Don't Count out Colton Joseph Just Yet Skip to main content SI.COM WISCONSIN ATHLETICS FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS FOOTBALL BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS BASKETBALL As the Badgers' seesaw of a 2026 season rolls on, Wisconsin once finds itself on the wrong end of a tough loss after collapsing on the road against Maryland . Sitting at 6-4 (4-3 in the B1G), head coach Luke Fickell and company are running out of time to prove that they're guiding this program in the right direction. A resounding win over an inferior opponent , bouncing back from a mind-numbing loss in the process, would be a great start. I've got three bold predictions for the Badgers' clash with the Boilermakers in West Lafayette. Colton Joseph recaptures the hearts of Badgers fans Wisconsin Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Hopkins is currently listed as questionable this week, but the early indications are that Joseph is going to re-assume the QB1 role after Hopkins took a huge blindside hit and had to be helped off the field late in the loss to Maryland. Ryan Hopkins is currently listed as questionable this week, but the early indications are that Joseph is going to re-assume the QB1 role after Hopkins took a huge blindside hit and had to be helped off the field late in the loss to Maryland. If Joseph indeed gets the starting nod in place of an injured Hopkins, it's not hard to see him playing well and in the process, winning back the hearts of some Badgers fans despite his well-documented struggles this season. First of all, Joseph should have no shortage of motivation. He was benched for a true freshman, and now gets his shot to prove that was a big mistake. That's a situation any competitor dreams of, and say what you will about Joseph; he's certainly a competitor. What's more, after getting benched for Hopkins and with the future of the entire coaching staff potentially up in the air this offseason, Joseph needs to put good things on tape should he be forced to enter the transfer portal again this winter. At best, he's proved dynamic yet inconsistent at the Big Ten level and at worst, he's been a turnover machine with limited arm talent. If Hopkins is forced to sit out one or both of the final two games this fall, these contests are massively important for Joseph's future; how he plays could determine whether he remains at the Power Four level in 2027. Finally, Purdue's defense is extremely permeable . It has the worst total defense in the Big Ten (417.3 yards per game) and the second-worst passing defense in the conference (239.0 yards per game). Purdue struggles to get consistent pressure (13 sacks across 10 games) and doesn't force turnovers with regularity. If there's any defense for Joseph to carve through, it's the Boilermakers. Purdue Boilermakers quarterback Ryan Browne. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Purdue's Ryan Browne is second in the Big Ten and 20th nationally with 2,418 passing yards. Though Purdue scores 27.2 points per game, a meager 76th in the country, its quarterback has been a bright spot in terms of offensive production. Purdue's Ryan Browne is second in the Big Ten and 20th nationally with 2,418 passing yards. Though Purdue scores 27.2 points per game, a meager 76th in the country, its quarterback has been a bright spot in terms of offensive production. Still, dive into Browne's performance this season, and the numbers are a tad misleading. The quarterback hasn't eclipsed 300 passing yards since Week 3 against UCLA, and while that's certainly an impressive feat given how strong the Bruins' defense is, he's struggled pretty mightily against the other top defenses he's faced. In fact, Browne has been held under 160 passing yards in four of his last seven outings. Against the top passing defenses he's played such as Penn State (No. 3 nationally in passing yards allowed per game) as well as Iowa and Minnesota (both of whom rank inside the top-45 in passing yards allowed), he's had a rough go of it. The Nittany Lions held him to 142 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions on 34 percent completion. Iowa limited him to 158 yards, one touchdown and one interceptions. And while Purdue blew out Minnesota, Brown only collected 159 passing yards, one score and 58 percent completion. Wisconsin's pass defense, meanwhile, checks in at No. 25 in the country. And while it just allowed Maryland's backup to complete 21-of-23 passes last week, the Badgers' defense has managed to bounce back from its poor performances this season. It'll need to run it back in West Lafayette. The Badgers' offensive line looks passable This might be the boldest prediction of the three, considering how much of a struggle its been up front for Wisconsin. Last week against Maryland, the Badgers' offensive line struggled mightily in pass protection, allowing four sacks. It wasn't much better in the run game, as Wisconsin backs created just 3.3 yards per carry and also suffered six tackles-for-loss. Still, Maryland's lowly record did well to disguise just how capable its front seven actually is. For how bad the Terps have been this fall, their defensive front is pretty loaded with capable playmakers. The same can't be said for Purdue. The Boilermakers have just 13 sacks on the season, firmly placing them into the bottom tier of teams; only 14 FBS programs have fewer. They've created 107 total pressures, which is harder to contextualize nationally but compared with Wisconsin's 145 total pressures, they're a clear step down. Their run defense, meanwhile, surrenders 178.3 yards per game, good for 110th nationally. Their defense as a whole has collected 205 stops, or tackles that constitute a failure for the offense, compared to Wisconsin's 276. Translation? They don't penetrate the backfield or win at the point of attack nearly as well as the Badgers. Despite what could be a patchwork offensive line this week, I still expect Wisconsin to find success up front. The undefeated fifth-ranked Boilermakers led No. 10 Wisconsin 17-14 in a nationally televised game (back when that wasn't the norm) and with ESPN College Gameday set up on campus. Kyle Orton ran a naked bootleg on third down, seemingly keeping the drive alive for Purdue to burn more clock, only Orton was hit, jarring the ball loose. Scott Starks picked it up and returned it 40 yards for a touchdown. After Bernard Pollard blocked the extra point, the Boilers drove into field goal range but missed a game-tying field goal attempt in the final minute. Wisconsin escaped Ross-Ade Stadium with a 20-17 victory , its first in what is now a string of 18 consecutive Badger victories in the series. On Saturday, Purdue coach Barry Odom gets his first chance to end more than two decades of coming up on the wrong side against the Badgers . away.headline: Ryan Hopkins headlines first Wisconsin vs. Purdue availability report
away.blurb: However, Luke Fickell and Co. didn’t just leave SECU Stadium with a bruised ego, as newly-donned starting quarterback Ryan Hopkins was recently listed as questionable in Wisconsin’s latest injury availability report ahead of this weekend’s clash against the Purdue Boilermakers . The Wisconsin Badgers are stumbling to the end of the 2026 football season, as their 24-21 loss against the Maryland Terrapins last weekend did them no favors. What does this mean for Wisconsin’s quarterback situation? In Hopkins’ two starts for the Badgers , the Mater Dei product tallied 318 yards through the air, on a 63% completion rate, along with three touchdowns and two fumbles. In Wisconsin’s last-second loss to the Terps, Hopkins finished with just 55 yards in the air, continuing a trend of disappointing quarterback play in 2026. If Hopkins is unable to go, it's plausible that original starter Colton Joseph gets the start, as the former Old Dominion quarterback has totaled 1,739 all-purpose yards, along with 15 total touchdowns and six turnovers. away.headline: Wisconsin football gets bad news on Javan Robinson, O-line from initial Purdue injury report
away.blurb: With two games to play in the regular season, however, that luck may be running out . Wisconsin's initial injury report lists starting cornerback and the Badgers' best cover man in the secondary, Javan Robinson, as doubtful for Saturday afternoon. That means barring a significant development, Wisconsin will be without its top cornerback and another veteran leader in the secondary. Starting quarterback Ryan Hopkins, who Fickell sounded encouraged about on Monday, is listed as questionable. Right now, it looks like a toss-up if he'll be able to play despite Fickell saying earlier in the week that "Hopefully he'll be fine...luckily it's not his throwing side." Wisconsin's starting right tackle Emerson Mandell is also listed as questionable. He wasn't noticeably banged up last week against the Terps, so Fickell wasn't asked about his status on Monday. However, he's now a question mark as well, and with Barrett Nelson also unavailable for the past three weeks, Wisconsin could be forced to start a tackle tandem of PJ Wilkins and Lucas Simmons-Johansson. That's certainly less than ideal, although the latter did just play a career-high 26 snaps against Maryland. Though Robinson almost certainly being out and the uncertainty around Hopkins and Mandell is disheartening, the Badgers did receive some good news on the injury front. Their other starting cornerback Jai'mier Scott, who didn't play last week in College Park, is listed as probable, as is star pass-rusher Sebastian Cheeks. Getting those two back would do wonders to mitigate the damage this defense has already suffered. Regardless of how the week shakes out, Wisconsin is going to have to take down Purdue somewhat short-handed. Wisconsin Football is Running Out of Time to Fix its Ground Game Other than the constant shuffling on the offensive line, much of which was caused at least initially by injuries suffered before the season began, Wisconsin football has had a relatively clean bill of health for much of the year, especially considering head coach Luke Fickell's past injury luck in Madison. When Wisconsin (6-4, 4-3 B1G) travels to face Purdue (3-7, 2-5 B1G) on Saturday afternoon in West Lafayette, it could be without several key starters in a game that's critically important for Fickell and company to bounce back and win after the late collapse in College Park last weekend. We already knew that starting safety Matt Jung was lost for the season, joining the likes of offensive tackle Kevin Heywood and cornerback Cai Bates. But the Badgers' initial injury report poses more questions than answers ahead of a game against Purdue in which, again, Wisconsin could really use a bounce-back victory on the road. Status of key starters in question vs. Boilermakers That's especially relevant this week, as Purdue quarterback Ryan Browne is second in the Big Ten with 2,418 passing yards. The Boilermakers also have some dangerous wide receivers, although their leading pass-catcher Asaad Waseem is primarily a slot

Latest bowl projections before Virginia game INJURY REPORT: Who is on UNC football vs Virginia injury report? Latest from ACC availability report POSTGAME BRAWL: ACC announces suspensions, fines for UNC football and Louisville after postgame fight UNC has a 4-1 record away from Chapel Hill this season, including a season-opening win against TCU in Ireland. The Tar Heels have won three straight road games since a mid-September loss at Clemson. UNC has also won consecutive games on Virginia's home field. If it stretches that streak to three, it would be the first time since 2016. Overall, the Tar Heels have a 28-27 record at Virginia. Here are some stats to know, players to watch and a score prediction for the Tar Heels vs. Cavaliers. Billy Edwards or Travis Burgess as UNC quarterback vs Virginia? Who will be UNC's starting quarterback vs. Virginia? That's the biggest question surrounding this game. A sixth-year player who started the first 10 games of the season, Billy Edwards Jr. was listed as questionable on the initial ACC availability report . That could open the door for freshman QB Travis Burgess to get his first career start. Burgess replaced Edwards in the second half of the Tar Heels' loss to Louisville, leading a late scoring drive that gave UNC an opportunity to win in the fourth quarter. If Burgess does get the start, he would be the first true freshman to start at QB for UNC in an ACC game since Sam Howell in 2019. UNC defense faces challenge vs Virginia QB Beau Pribula without Greg Smith UNC's defense is arguably coming off its best performance of the season, limiting a Louisville offense that averaged more than 40 points per game to 16 at Kenan Stadium. The Tar Heels won't face that level of explosiveness against Virginia, but it could be tough because of the absence of two key players. Defensive back Greg Smith and defensive lineman Melkart Abou Jaoude are among the Tar Heels out vs. the Cavaliers, but Smith is only out for the first half for his role in the postgame brawl vs. Louisville. In Virginia's wins, quarterback Beau Pribula is averaging 171 passing yards and 45 rushing yards with 11 passing TDs, one rushing TD and one interception. In five losses, Pribula is averaging 174 passing yards and 7 rushing yards with four passing TDs, two interceptions and a rushing TD. If UNC can bottle up Pribula, it'll likely leave Charlottesville its sixth win of the season. UNC running back Benjamin Hall gets redemption shot vs Virginia Benjamin Hall was just short of the goal line on a two-point conversion that would have given UNC its first signature win under Bill Belichick in 2025. The Tar Heels lost 17-16 to No. 16 Virginia in overtime last season at Kenan Stadium . With three touchdowns in the last two weeks, including a two-TD effort vs. Louisville, Hall will have a chance at redemption on Saturday at Scott Stadium. The junior running back's two best games of the season came on the road. Hall logged 130 rushing yards and a receiving TD at Clemson and racked up 81 rushing yards and a TD on nine carries at UConn. UNC vs Virginia score prediction UNC 22, Virginia 18: The Tar Heels have been a different team on the road this season, finding ways to win by creating takeaways and scoring on explosive plays. Even with its questions at QB, UNC seems to get a jolt away from Chapel Hill. Belichick's boys will be celebrating in Charlottesville after securing bowl eligibility ahead of the regular-season finale. picks.blurb: North Carolina vs Virginia Prediction 11/21/2026 Today's College Football Picks - Pick Dawgz Pick Dawgz North Carolina vs Virginia Prediction 11/21/2026 Today’s College Football Picks Chris Ruffolo 4 hours ago Nov 14, 2026; Chapel Hill, North Carolina, USA; Louisville Cardinals defensive back Koen Entringer (5) causes North Carolina Tar Heels quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. (9) to fumble in the second quarter at Kenan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images North Carolina Tar Heels Virginia Cavaliers Over 42.5 (-105) Under 42.5 (-115) Scott Stadium, Charlottesville, VA Saturday, November 21, 2026 North Carolina Tar Heels vs. Virginia Cavaliers Prediction I’m taking North Carolina and the points against Virginia. Both teams are 5-5 and need one more win to get bowl eligible, but I think the Tar Heels are in the better spot, even on the road. Virginia finally put together a convincing performance against Cal, and congratulations on that, but one good Saturday doesn’t erase how rough conference play has been for the Cavaliers. North Carolina hasn’t exactly been reliable at home, either. The difference is that the Tar Heels have actually played some of their best football away from Chapel Hill, and I think that travels to Charlottesville. North Carolina is 3-1 in true road games, with wins at Pitt, Duke and UConn. The Pitt and Duke wins came by four points apiece, and the Tar Heels followed them with a 38-21 victory at UConn. That’s not a murderer’s row, but winning three straight road games is hard to dismiss when we’re talking about a matchup priced essentially as a toss-up. Compare that with North Carolina’s recent home form: losses to Syracuse, Miami and Louisville in three of its last four games. The results haven’t always been pretty, but the road version of this team has been more dependable. Virginia’s 36-7 win over Cal looks great on the scoreboard, although it’s worth remembering that two of the Cavaliers’ touchdowns came on interception returns. That was a much-needed response after losing three straight to SMU, Duke and Wake Forest, including a 51-7 beating at Wake. I’ve been waiting for Virginia’s veteran offensive line to become a consistent strength, but it hasn’t happened. The Cavaliers have struggled to protect Beau Pribula and are converting only about 32 percent of third downs. That’s a major problem against a North Carolina defense that just showed it can make a good offense work. The Tar Heels lost 16-14 to Louisville last week, but I thought the defense deserved a lot more credit than the final result suggests. Louisville came in averaging more than 40 points and nearly eight yards per play. North Carolina held the Cardinals to 302 yards, just 4.7 per play, and only one gain of more than 20 yards. Derek McDonald has been all over the field with 101 tackles on the season. If that defense shows up again, Virginia isn’t suddenly going to find easy yards just because it’s playing its home finale. There is one legitimate concern for North Carolina, and that’s the quarterback situation. Billy Edwards Jr. left the Louisville game injured and was listed as questionable, while freshman Travis Burgess came in and showed some mobility but also threw an interception. I’m not going to pretend that uncertainty doesn’t matter. Still, Virginia has been vulnerable to mobile quarterbacks, and Burgess at least gives the Tar Heels a different way to move the chains if he’s needed. North Carolina is also converting around 46 percent of its third downs, compared with Virginia’s much lower rate, which is a meaningful difference in a game where possessions could be limited. Virginia is 5-1 at Scott Stadium, and this is Senior Day, so the Cavaliers absolutely have a home-field argument. Pribula can hurt opponents with his legs, too, and Virginia’s plus-six turnover margin is better than North Carolina’s minus-three. Those are real reasons this isn’t a slam dunk. But the Cavaliers have struggled to finish drives, scoring on roughly 73 percent of their red-zone trips, while North Carolina has converted better than 90 percent of its opportunities. With neither offense consistently explosive, missed chances inside the twenty could matter as much as the occasional big play. Chris Ruffolo's Pick: North Carolina +1.5

The North Carolina Tar Heels are off to a 3-1 start to the 2026-27 season in their first year under head coach Michael Malone. It's a solid start for Malone's team, but they are dealing with a disappointing injury, as guard Neo Avdalas is expected to miss at least two months with a broken wrist . In four games with the Tar Heels, Avdalas averaged nine points, 3.5 rebounds, and 3.8 assists per game, shooting 40.6 percent from the field and 20 percent from three. He was going to be a key playmaker for North Carolina and will be a significant absence in their lineup over the next couple of months. Avdalas spent his freshman season at Virginia Tech, averaging 12.1 points, 3.1 rebounds, and 4.6 assists per game, shooting 38.6 percent from the floor and 31.4 percent from deep. It was a solid freshman campaign, and he was poised to be a pivotal piece in the Tar Heels' rotation. During his absence, North Carolina will lean on Isaiah Denis, Matt Able, and Terrence Brown to step up as playmakers. Able will also play a key role as a playmaker, as he's averaging 10.8 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 2.3 assists per game, shooting 44.1 percent from the floor and 30.4 percent from downtown. He is a solid scorer, but they will need him to pick up his playmaking over the next couple of months. North Carolina's top scorer, Brown, could also be needed to step up as a passer. He is averaging 17.5 points, 3.5 rebounds, 1.5 assists, and two steals per game, shooting 43.4 percent from the field and 38.5 percent from distance. North Carolina is looking to make a deep run in Malone's first year as their head coach. Malone had a successful tenure in the NBA, winning a championship with the Denver Nuggets. The Tar Heels went 24-9 in the 2025-26 season, but lost in the first round of the NCAA Tournament. North Carolina has a different roster and coaching staff this season and will look to be a contender to win the NCAA title, but will have to survive early in the season without Avdalas.

away.headline: North Carolina's Neo Avdalas to Miss Two Months With Wrist Injury
away.blurb: A potential two-month recovery timeline could put Avdalas in position to return around January, although North Carolina has not announced a specific return date. ACC Football Injury Report: Georgia Tech Lists 17 Out, Stanford 15 North Carolina's Neo Avdalas to Miss Two Months With Wrist Injury Football North Carolina basketball has suffered a significant setback early in the 2026-27 season, as sophomore guard Neo Avdalas is expected to miss approximately two months after suffering a fractured left wrist. The Tar Heels announced Tuesday that Avdalas underwent surgery to repair the injury. The sophomore suffered the injury during Friday night’s 78-70 loss to Georgia at the Dean E. Smith Center. Avdalas is expected to miss a significant portion of North Carolina’s nonconference schedule, along with the beginning of ACC play, as he begins his recovery. The injury is a tough blow for first-year head coach Michael Malone, who has relied on Avdalas as an important part of the Tar Heels’ backcourt rotation. Through North Carolina’s first four games, Avdalas averaged 9.0 points, 3.5 rebounds and a team-leading 3.8 assists per game. He also recorded 15 assists, the most on the team, while ranking fourth in scoring. Avdalas started all four games for the Tar Heels after transferring from Virginia Tech during the offseason. During his freshman season with the Hokies, the 6-foot-9 guard averaged 12.1 points and 4.6 assists per game. He started all 31 games and earned ACC Rookie of the Week honors twice. His size, versatility and playmaking ability made him an important addition to Malone’s first North Carolina roster. Tar Heels Must Adjust Without Neo Avdalas With Avdalas sidelined, North Carolina will need other players to take on additional responsibilities in the backcourt. Terrence Brown, Isaiah Denis, Angelo Brizzi and Jaydon Young could all see increased opportunities as the Tar Heels look to replace Avdalas’ production and playmaking. Brown has been one of North Carolina’s leading offensive contributors early in the season, while Denis has also provided valuable minutes in the backcourt. North Carolina enters the next stretch of its schedule at 3-1 following the loss to Georgia. The Tar Heels will look to get back on track when they host Marshall on Friday, Nov. 20. His absence will be an early test for Malone and the Tar Heels as they attempt to maintain momentum and navigate the opening portion of their ACC schedule without one of their key offseason additions. home.blurb: The ACC released the initial injury reports for this weekend's contests, and, unsurprisingly, starting quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. is listed as questionable. While we all expected Edwards Jr. to be listed as questionable, given his status for Saturday is still very much in question, we did find out that two defensive standouts already have been ruled out. #UNC football’s initial availability report for its game at Virginia. The surprise is DB Greg Smith III: He was set to receive a one-half suspension by the ACC for his role in fight after the Tar Heels’ loss to Louisville, but now is listed as OUT entirely. pic.twitter.com/9ZEtghMPBD Melkart Abou Jaoude, who has dealt with injuries all season long, has already been ruled out for UNC's second-to-last regular-season game. Greg Smith III , who was suspended for the first half of the game after being involved in a postgame brawl last weekend, has also been ruled out. Virginia has an extensive list of players already ruled out for Saturday afternoon's clash against UNC. In total, 13 players have already been ruled out, as the injury bug could force more to be sidelined before kickoff occurs in just a few days. The story to follow for UNC will be Edwards Jr.'s status. Because he was limited in practice, there's some doubt he'll be able to play against the Cavaliers, but it all depends on how the rest of the week shapes up. If he's unable to go, expect true freshman Travis Burgess, who came in relief following Edwards Jr.'s injury against Louisville, to make his first collegiate start. The No. 4 Bruins are arriving for their first game at Michigan Stadium since 1996 on Saturday in prime position to reach the Big Ten Championship Game and College Football Playoff. The Wolverines team hosting them is scraping rock bottom after falling to 5-5 with a 31-7 loss at Oregon last week. It's a jarring backdrop for the first battle between these teams as Big Ten foes. At 10-0 (7-0 Big Ten), the Bruins are one win away from reaching 11 victories for the first time in program history. Just three years removed from a national championship, Michigan may be on the cusp of yet another coaching change. Lauded as a stabilizing hire amid a tumultuous ending to Sherrone Moore's tenure last year, Whittingham has presided over a disaster. Michigan ranks 131st of 138 FBS teams in total offense, averaging just 300.9 yards per game. While the Wolverines have quickly reached dire straits under Whittingham, 66, they can play the role of spoiler over the season's final two weeks. Handing UCLA its first loss and/or upsetting rival Ohio State to close the season would bring some morsel of satisfaction to what has been a painful 2026 slog in Ann Arbor. Michigan lost on the road against Oregon, 31-7, last weekend, and it didn't look like anyone was mentally present for the Wolverines. This weekend presents a new challenge — the UCLA Bruins. UCLA is having a special season, especially considering this was one of the worst teams in the Big Ten last year. The Bruins are 10-0 and knocking on the doorstep of the Big Ten Championship and College Football Playoff. A win this weekend would clinch the Bruins a spot in Indy, and it would likely make it impossible for them to miss the CFP. Somehow, UCLA is only favored by 3.5 points leading up to this game. Does Vegas know something, or will it be another uninspiring performance from the Wolverines? Let's make some bold predictions for the game. Michigan will go to another backup QB The Oregon game was interesting, as Michigan went back-and-forth between Tommy Carr and Bryce Underwood, waiting for someone to provide a spark. The thing is, I really don't think it matters. I don't think the issue is with the quarterbacks at all, as I think Underwood and Carr have both shown some good flashes. I believe the real issue boils down to poor offensive line play and the refusal to involve the tight ends more. Still, the coaches are going to search for a spark. Brayden Fowler-Nicolosi, a transfer from Colorado State, should be next in line at the quarterback position. I'm honestly surprised we haven't seen him yet, but there's truly nothing to lose at this point. Give him a shot. Michigan gets shutout I don't like to reuse predictions in these, but I'm honestly shocked this hasn't happened yet and I feel like it's inevitable at this point. This offense has amazed us with levels of bad we didn't know existed, and I think it still has one more trick up its sleeve. UCLA is 10-0 in large part due to its defense. Remember, the Bruins have been without starting quarterback Nico Iamaleava since Oct. 10 when he got hurt at Oregon. Since then, only one team has hit 20 points against the Bruins. They are ranked No. 4 in the country in total defense. UCLA is shutting everyone down. Michigan barely avoided a shutout against Michigan State, a bad team with a bad defense. The Wolverines haven't been shutout at home since 1967, but that could change this weekend. UCLA wins, 17-0 UCLA is great defensively, but the Bruins have only eclipsed 30 points once with Ty Dieffenbach at quarterback, so I expect Michigan's defense to keep this one relatively close. Still, I just can't imagine the Wolverines finding any success offensively, and I would be shocked if UCLA doesn't easily cover the spread. Michigan's bowl hopes will hinge on The Game.

away.blurb: Kiffin's return to Tennessee He did not come out with the rest of the team out of halftime and did not return to the game to start the third quarter. UCLA's backup quarterback is Madden Iamaleava, the younger brother of Nico Iamaleava. He's in his second season with the Bruins and has seen limited action in his college career. Ty Dieffenbach injury updates: UCLA QB returns after exiting in first half after hard hit - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF 'GTA 6' impacts sports Jordan Mendoza, USA TODAY · USA TODAY Sports Sat, November 14, 2026 at 3:53 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads PASADENA, CA — UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach suffered an injury on a hard hit late in the first half against Illinois on Friday, Nov. 13. But it appears to not be an absolutely devastating hit for the Bruins . With 35 seconds left in the second quarter, Dieffenbach tried to throw the ball away when he got tripped up and was clearly in immediate pain. He was visibly shaken as he was attended to by support staff, and he appeared to indicate he had a left shoulder injury. After a few minutes he was helped up and taken to the sideline. Once the teams headed to the locker room, Dieffenbach went in appearing to not move his left arm and was limping. Ty Dieffenbach latest injury news Dieffenbach suffered an "upper body injury," according to the Fox broadcast. However, he emerged from the locker room with about four minutes left in the third quarter with a sleeve on his left arm, as the Rose Bowl crowd cheered. Dieffenbach was back on the field for UCLA late in the third quarter and played the remainder of the game. "I kind of went down a little awkward on the tackle, and my arm got caught up underneath, but it just got a little tight on me, and it's nothing serious," he said postgame. The Bruins got their quarterback to engineer another win. He reignited the offense, throwing a key fourth quarter touchdown to Semaj Morgan that strengthened the lead. UCLA held on to beat Illinois 22-14 to move to 10-0. Dieffenbach went 13-for-20 for 232 yards with two touchdowns and one interception, with 28 rushing yards. The injury was a big scare to UCLA's quarterback room as Dieffenbach has played in place of starter Nico Iamaleava after Iamaleava suffered a season ending injury against Oregon on Oct. 10. Dieffenbach has stepped up and kept the Bruins one of two undefeated teams left in the country, at 9-0 for the first time since 1998 with a shot at their first College Football Playoff appearance. Prior to the injury, Dieffenbach was 8-for-13 for 168 yards with one touchdown and one interception, leading UCLA to a 10-0 lead over Illinois. It was the Tigers' fourth loss of the season, they're out of the College Football Playoff mix, and now it's time to play the spoiler role. Kiffin gets to play the villain, going back to his old coaching grounds – he was the Tennessee head coach in 2009 – and Tennessee will be fired up. The Vols are 8-2 after winning five of their last six games, and at No. 9 in the latest rankings, they're all but in the CFP if they win their last two games. LSU vs Tennessee: Quick Hits LSU closes out on the road at Arkansas after this. Lose to the Vols, and it'll be the third year in a row the program suffered a three-game losing streak. Tennessee goes to Vanderbilt to finish up the regular season. If it wins the final two games, it's in the mix for the SEC Championship along with the CFP. The two programs haven't met since 2022 – a 40-13 Tennessee win. LSU has won five of the last six, going back to 2005. LSU isn't going anywhere this season, and now it can be Lane Unleashed as the team throws everything at a Vols team with all of the weight on its side of the field. The defense is the best in the SEC, the offense is the best in the SEC, the team holds the ball longer than anyone else in the conference, and no one in America generates more sacks. Tennessee has a problem keeping defenses out of the backfield, and now, here come the Tigers. Why Tennessee Will Win LSU might generate the most sacks in America, but Tennessee can bring the heat, too – the Tigers are No. 2 in sacks. It didn't sack Marcel Reed in last week's 22-7 win over Texas A&M, but it gave him a rough time. Now the Vols are back at home, where they take their defensive production up several notches. The defense has allowed just one touchdown pass in five games in Neyland, but in this, it's about the Tennessee run defense. LSU is 1-3 when running for fewer than 140 yards. Auburn and Furman – the Vols called off the dogs against the Paladins – are the only teams to hit the 140-yard mark. LSU vs Tennessee Prediction, Betting Lines Here's the thing about LSU this season. It pounces on the weak, but its best win is … at Auburn? That's good, but there really isn't a second-best victory going 0-4 against the current CFP-ranked teams on the slate. Tennessee is a top team. This might not be the sexiest team going, but it's got grit. It's a tough defensive team that doesn't make a ton of mistakes, and it doesn't get rattled. LSU will be terrific, but like the Kentucky and Texas games, it'll crumble late in the final moments. Tennessee's College Football Playoff hopes are on the line this weekend against LSU. If the Vols beat LSU on Saturday in Neyland Stadium, they'll just need a win in the regular-season finale against Vanderbilt to lock down a spot in the College Football Playoff. But if Tennessee loses to LSU, they can likely kiss their playoff hopes goodbye. LSU, which has four losses, is out of the playoff picture. The Tigers' 6-4 record, however, isn't indicative of how good of a team they are. LSU has arguably the most talented roster in the nation, and they are just a couple of plays away from being 8-2. Tennessee has a 59% chance to make the College Football Playoff and a 4% chance to win the national title, according to the A to Z Sports CFB Playoff Predictor (updated November 15, 2026). Combine that with the fact that Tennessee will be without several key players against the Tigers — specifically left guard Nic Moore and wide receiver Mike Matthews — and it's easy to see why there's some concern about this game on Rocky Top. Former Georgia QB Aaron Murray makes his prediction for LSU vs Tennessee Former Georgia quarterback Aaron Murray predicted last week that Tennessee would beat Texas A&M by 13 points last week (the Vols won by 15 points), but he's not making the same kind of prediction for the LSU game. Murray has the Tigers taking down the Vols on Saturday, predicting that LSU will leave Neyland Stadium with a 23-17 win. One of the main reasons Murray is predicting an LSU win is because the Vols will be without Mike Matthews. "This (LSU) defense is going to be able to put you in third-and-long situations," said Murray. "And they're going to be able to get to the quarterback with Princewill Umanmielen and Jordan Ross coming off the edge. "… Can Tennessee's offense, without Matthews and with a banged up quarterback — it's possibly Faizon Brandon back in there playing quarterback — get the job done against LSU in this matchup? I don't feel very confident. Which is why I'm going with LSU 23-17 in this football game. If Mike Matthews was healthy, and if [George MacIntyre] — I don't know what the knee is right now, maybe he's 100 percent for the game [and I would feel different]. But still, no Mike Matthews. I think that's a big problem for the Tennessee Volunteers. So I think LSU wins the game." I think that's a fair prediction from Murray. There are certainly questions about the Vols' offense without Matthews. The junior wide receiver was easily Tennessee's most dynamic playmaker. But LSU has failed to finish games in the fourth quarter this season and that's an area where Tennessee has thrived. If the Vols can get this game to the fourth quarter, I like their chances. But if they get to the fourth quarter and they're down multiple scores, it could be too big of a hill for Tennessee's offense to climb. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. picks.headline: ‘Tennessee is hurt everywhere' – Former Georgia star David Pollack predicts who will win the important matchup between LSU and Tennessee

Tennessee has dealt with terrible injury luck this season — the Vols have had 10 season-ending injuries — but they're still in contention for a College Football Playoff spot with two weeks remaining in the regular season. All Tennessee needs to do is beat LSU and Vanderbilt and they'll lock up a spot in the playoff. First up is LSU. The Tigers are 6-4 and out of the playoff conversation, but they have a talented and dangerous roster that is as good as any team in the nation when they're at their best. Former Georgia pass rusher David Pollack makes prediction for LSU vs Tennessee Former Georgia standout David Pollack made his pick for the matchup between the Vols and the Tigers. Tennessee has a 59% chance to make the College Football Playoff and a 4% chance to win the national title, according to the A to Z Sports CFB Playoff Predictor (updated November 15, 2026). Pollack likes what he's seen from Tennessee this season, but he thinks the Volunteers have too many injuries to win this game. So, Pollack has LSU winning by a field goal. "Tennessee is hurt everywhere," said Pollack . "Tennessee's beat to death. If Tennessee wins this game, holy cow, man. I mean, that's how much the injuries have been such a big issue for them across the board. Whether it's the quarterback, Mike Matthews at wide receiver, the offensive line, a pass rusher — Tennessee's lost a significant player at almost every spot on the field. That's hard to overcome. "… They've (LSU) been in these games. It's been competitive, and it's been different ways they've beaten themselves. I think the injuries just eat up Tennessee, and I think LSU finds a way to make a few more plays with the ability of Sam Leavitt to scramble against this defensive line. And I think [LSU's] ability to run tempo and kind of wear you out — Tennessee can do the same exact thing, but I think LSU's got more bodies. I just think they've got more availability. I think this is a low-scoring affair — like every Tennessee game is — but I think LSU wins by a field goal." If it's a close game late, I like Tennessee's chances better than LSU's — simply because the Vols have been better at closing games in the fourth quarter than the Tigers have. But I agree with Pollack that Tennessee's injuries are a concern. The Vols have lost a significant number of playmakers, and losing Mike Matthews, Tennessee's top offensive playmaker, is a massive concern against an offense like LSU's. I mean, this is a game where the Vols are probably going to have to throw it a bit more than they have in most games this season in order to win. Can they do that without Matthews? The one thing I'll say about Tennessee this season is that every time they've had an injury, the next man up has delivered. So I'm not doubting Tennessee's ability to get it done against LSU, I just wonder if they'll be healthy enough to find a way. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. away.headline: LSU loses defensive captain before Lane Kiffin’s return to Tennessee
away.blurb: The Tigers ruled out senior defensive captain Whit Weeks on their Thursday availability report, according to on3 , changing his designation from doubtful a day earlier. LSU (6-4, 3-4 SEC ) visits No. 9 Tennessee (8-2, 5-2) in the Volunteers’ final regular-season college football home game. Tennessee coach Josh Heupel singled out LSU’s pass rush on Monday. The Tigers enter Saturday with a national-best 40 sacks and Heupel pointed to their ability to generate pressure with different players and packages. Lane Kiffin will be back on the visiting sideline at Neyland Stadium on Saturday. He’ll coach his first NCAA game there for LSU without the linebacker he chose to wear the Tigers’ No. 7. The report applies to Saturday’s game and does not establish whether Weeks will play again this season. Weeks has not played since he broke his lower right leg against Texas A&M on Sept. 26. He missed LSU’s 22-21 loss to Texas last week despite making it to game day with a chance to play. In four games this season, Weeks recorded 23 tackles, including 2.5 for loss. Weeks earned first-team all-conference honors after making 125 tackles in 2024, second most in the SEC. LSU named him a permanent captain last season, when another lower-leg injury cost him five games. Before this season, Kiffin picked Weeks and tight end Trey’Dez Green to wear No. 7, a number the program reserves for prominent players. Who Has Filled In For Whit Weeks? Junior linebacker Davhon Keys has taken on more work in Weeks’ absence. Keys led LSU in tackles with 92 last season and started four of its final seven games while filling in for Weeks. He led the Tigers with nine tackles against Texas, including 1.5 for loss. Fellow starting linebacker TJ Dottery had six. The Tigers forced three interceptions against Texas and took a 21-10 lead into the fourth quarter. They still lost when Arch Manning found Raleek Brown for a 4-yard touchdown in the final seconds. Tennessee scored 19 unanswered points in a 22-7 road win over Texas A&M. The Volunteers are ninth in the latest College Football Playoff committee rankings and are trying to hold their place in the field. It doesn't matter – as long as the Irish win, they'll end up in the tournament. But drop a game over the last two weeks, and all CFP bets are off. SMU had its chance last week to all but land a spot in the ACC Championship, but one 49-7 rocking from Wake Forest later, and now it's looking to play spoiler to Notre Dame's season. Notre Dame vs SMU: Quick Hits SMU not only got blown out by Wake Forest, but that was the final home game. The Mustangs close out at Stanford. Notre Dame still has to deal with a road game at Syracuse to close things out. These two haven't played since 1989 – a 59-6 Notre Dame win. The Irish are 10-3 in the series going back to 1930. How To Watch Notre Dame vs SMU Date: Saturday, November 21, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: NBC Location: Notre Dame Stadium, Notre Dame, IN – Week 12 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 25 – CFN Week 12 Expert Picks Why SMU Will Win SMU is still a dangerous team, even after the disaster against the Demon Deacons. The offense is terrific, with a great pace and balance that can be impossible to stop when it gets into a rhythm. Notre Dame hasn't faced too many sharp passing teams, but there was a problem against the stronger quarterbacks. BYU's Bear Bachmeier hit 65% of his passes in the 28-24 win, and Miami's Darian Mensah almost pulled the game out of the fire, throwing for 269 yards and three scores. One loss, one close call, and those were the two times the Irish allowed more than 300 total yards. SMU has one of the nation's most efficient passing games for an offense that averages 456 yards per game. Why Notre Dame Will Win How did Wake Forest destroy SMU? It came out roaring, and it was over. The Demon Deacons cranked up the pass rush against a leaky SMU line, and the three takeaways made things ugly. Yes, SMU works with a pace, but when it doesn't work, everything fizzes. But it's about the takeaways. SMU is 2-3 when turning it over multiple times, with 14 turnovers packed into those five games, and with nine turnovers in the three road games. Notre Dame is sixth in the nation in takeaways with 20. Notre Dame vs SMU Prediction, Betting Lines Yes, the Mustangs have a fun offense, and the quick-hitting style will hit the Irish defense for a few scores to throw a scare into the fan base for a half, but CJ Carr and the Notre Dame passing game are pretty good, too. Between the turnovers and lots of penalties, SMU isn't perfect. A few good drives will stall with giveaways, and even though the pass rush will get to Carr on a few third downs, the Irish will be locked in. They'll take over and pull away in the second half. But SMU has a chance to right a few wrongs this weekend, and play spoiler , traveling to South Bend to play Notre Dame. Here's how the ACC games might play out this weekend. Mandatory Credit: Michael Caterina-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) There aren't too many offenses more dynamic than SMU's. Kevin Jennings has already thrown for more than 2,900 yards this season and there are playmakers all over the field for Rhett Lashlee's team. But SMU has the second-most turnovers in the ACC, giving the ball up 15 times in 10 games. That's not winning football, and playing against a team like Notre Dame, with a veteran quarterback like CJ Carr, won't win you that game. SMU was thrashed against Wake Forest last weekend, and it was due to too many mistakes and the defense not stopping Gio Lopez. Carr has just two interceptions this season and if Jennings and Co. make mistakes, the Irish could turn the rout on. Notre Dame should be able to run the football against the Mustangs, too. The only way this game is close is if SMU scores quickly and gains some confidence and belief that it can win this game. Their last meeting didn't go too well for the visiting Mustangs as the Irish won 59-6 and took their foot off the gas relatively early in the second half. This year, however, it's a different looking SMU team that travels up north. This program is two years removed from playing for the ACC title and making the first ever 12-team College Football Playoffs. They have talent littered all over the field and will look to play spoiler to Notre Dame's Senior Day and their College Football Playoff hopes. Location : Notre Dame Stadium (Notre Dame, Ind.) Date : Saturday - November 21 Time : 7:30 PM ET TV : NBC/Peacock Line : Notre Dame -20.5; O/U 56.5 Let's kick off our preview of this matchup with an overview look at the SMU Mustangs Record at SMU : 45-19 (5th season) SMU head coach Rhett Lashlee is in the midst of his fifth season at the helm. Like the coach he's facing this Saturday, Marcus Freeman , he has had a winning record in every season he's been the head coach. In 2023 and 2024, the Mustangs posted back to back 11-3 seasons, playing for the ACC title in 2024 and making the College Football Playoffs. Unfortunately, they lost soundly on the road against Penn State but that didn't take away from the great season he had. Last year, expectations were at an all-time high for Lashlee and SMU and they entered as one of the favorites to win the league. Unfortunately, they ended their season at 9-4 and weren't able to handle business down the stretch to get back to the ACC title game. This year, SMU is looking similar to the 2025 version of themselves rather than the 2023 and 2024 versions, but a win over Notre Dame in South Bend could drastically change the outlook of their season. Lashlee has the talent to compete with some of the top teams in the country at certain spots, but he needs to put it all together to make it back to the CFP which likely won't happen this season. Offensive Coordinator : Rob Likens / Garin Justice / D'Eriq King Defensive Coordinator : Maurice Crum Jr . / Rickey Hunley Jr . 2026 STATISTICAL OVERVIEW STATISTICAL LEADERS Rushing : RB Kendrick Raphael - 165 att., 809 yards, 4.9 YPC, 10 TD; RB Christian Rhodes - 23 att., 171 yards, 7.4 YPC, 2 TD; RB Dramekco Green - 43 att., 152 yards, 3.5 YPC, 1 TD; QB Kevin Jennings - 68 att., 127 yards, 1.9 YPC, 2 TD Passing : QB Kevin Jennings - 231-318, 72.6%, 2,973 yards, 9.3 YPA, 26 TD, 7 INT, 173.3 Rating; QB Ty Hawkins - 12-14, 85.7%, 117 yards, 8.4 YPA, 2 TD; 203.4 Rating Receiving : WR Yamir Knight - 55 rec., 670 yards, 12.2 YPC, 6 TD; WR Yannick Smith - 34 rec., 540 yards, 15.9 YPC, 3 TD; WR Jalen Cooper - 34 rec., 498 yards, 14.6 YPC, 2 TD; TE Randy Pittman Jr. - 30 rec., 312 yards, 10.4 YPC, 4 TD; WR Jalen Hale - 19 rec., 272 yards, 14.3 YPC, 3 TD; TE Theo Melin Ohrstrom - 18 rec., 217 yards, 12.1 YPC, 4 TD; WR Derrick McFall - 9 rec., 167 yards, 18.6 YPC, 3 TD; RB Kendrick Raphael - 16 rec., 138 yards, 8.6 YPC, 1 TD Tackles : LB Alexander Kilgore - 57; LB Brandon Booker - 48; S Jimmy Wyrick - 45; S Sael Reyes - 44; S Tyren Polley Jr. - 34; CB Jayvon Thomas - 32; NB Jarvis Lee - 30; DE Marques White - 28; LB Jamal Anderson - 28; CB Marcellus Barnes - 26; LB Brandon Miyazono Tackles For Loss : DE Marques White - 12.0; NB Jarvis Lee - 6.5; DE Aakil Washington - 5.0; DT Christian Davis - 4.5; LB Brandon Booker - 4.0; LB Alexander Kilgore - 3.5; S Sael Reyes - 3.5; DT Malcolm Alcorn-Crowder - 3.0; LB Brandon Miyazono - 3.0; S Tyren Polley Jr. - 3.0 Interceptions : NB Jarvis Lee - 1; LB Brandon Booker - 1; S Jimmy Wyrick - 1 The talent that SMU has on their roster doesn't match their output over the last two seasons. After going a combined 22-6 from 2023 through 2024, they're now 16-7 from the start of 2025 through Week 11 of this year's college football season. Quarterback Kevin Jennings returned for his final year at the helm. In some ways, he's having the season many thought he would, but his abilities as a runner have not been utilized by the offensive coaching staff. To a degree, it's understandable given the talent on the perimeter with players like Yamir Knight , Jalen Cooper , Yannick Smith , Jalen Hale , Theo Melin Ohrstrom and Randy Pittman Jr. requiring a lot of touches. Their defense has been the area of struggle this season, as it was last season. In many areas, Maurice Crum Jr ., a former Notre Dame captain at linebacker, has changed the outlook of the defense for the better. But they're a 'feast or famine' type of unit ranking 13th in the country in tackles for loss and 20th in the country in sacks but also ranking 110th in the country in passing touchdowns allowed and 128th in the country in red zone scoring allowed. This season, when they've faced offenses that can score, they've allowed 41 points to Louisville, 30 points to Syracuse and 49 points to Wake Forest.
