picks.blurb: Notre Dame Fighting Irish vs SMU Mustangs Final Score Prediction Skip to content NFL Close Menu All NFL Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks College Football Close Menu All College Football Alabama Crimson Tide Auburn Tigers Florida Gators Georgia Bulldogs Miami Hurricanes Michigan Wolverines Notre Dame Fighting Irish Ohio State Buckeyes Oklahoma Sooners Ole Miss Rebels Penn State Nittany Lions Tennessee Volunteers Texas A&M Aggies Texas Longhorns Draft Simulator Trade Simulator CFB Playoff Predictor NFL Playoff Predictor Toggle Mobile Navigation Home College Football Notre Dame football hosts SMU in its final home game of the 2026 regular season. What should Fighting Irish fans expect in South Bend? Notre Dame football is two wins away from a College Football Playoff berth. The Fighting Irish host the SMU Mustangs at 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday in Notre Dame Stadium , and head coach Marcus Freeman's group needs to take care of business against SMU and then Syracuse to finish 11-1. It is also Senior Day. Hopefully the Irish land a home game in the playoff. Even so, this could be the last time this senior class walks out of the tunnel, hits the Play Like a Champion Today sign, and plays in front of the Notre Dame crowd. At one point, SMU looked like it would give Notre Dame's resume a nice bump. That changed after Wake Forest throttled the Mustangs last weekend. SMU trailed 42-0 at halftime and lost 49-7. This won't be the top-25 resume boost many expected, but Notre Dame still has plenty to play for. A decisive win could push the Irish up a couple more spots as the season winds down. Notre Dame is a 90% favorite to win outright in the Kalshi prediction market. The Irish are favored by 20.5 points, which is roughly three touchdowns, and Kalshi gives them a 51% chance of covering that number. I like both, and I especially like Notre Dame to cover. Don't expect a Senior Day hangover Some people will look at this game and point to Senior Day, a potential hangover, and the other usual distractions. I just find it unlikely that Notre Dame won't be locked in and ready to play. We had the same conversation heading into the Boston College game after the Irish beat No. 1 Miami. Notre Dame was cool, calm, and collected, and the team was ready early. Slow first halves have popped up occasionally during Freeman's tenure, but we didn't see one last week. SMU is also substantially better than Boston College. I don't want anyone to underrate the Mustangs because of the Wake Forest result. That game was a bit of an anomaly. This is still a quality 7-3 team, and if SMU had been on a bye last week, we would feel a whole lot different about this matchup. Should Notre Dame win convincingly? Absolutely. Can the Irish show up with their C or D game and cruise? I don't think so. Kevin Jennings and the SMU passing game SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings has been really good outside of a couple of bad games. He is one of the better passers in college football and has developed steadily over the last couple of years. He has some dual-threat ability, but he wants to stay inside of structure and win from the pocket. I don't think Jennings is going to have back-to-back stinkers. SMU has some good receivers on the outside, including Jaylen Cooper. Notre Dame fans may remember Cooper from the 2025 recruiting class, when the Irish tried to flip him from SMU. The Notre Dame secondary will be tested. The Irish are still without DJ McKinney, but will have Jayden Sanders and Leonard Moore available. There are obviously good pieces on the back end, but the Mustangs have the potential to create a couple of explosive plays in the passing game. What keeps SMU from scoring a ton of points is the run game. It has been wildly inconsistent. The Mustangs have run for 250 yards in some games and fewer than 100 in others. An offense that isn't balanced will struggle to sustain drives against a defense this good, and SMU's feast-or-famine passing attack figures to be spotty. What to watch from the Notre Dame offense SMU's offense can be dangerous, but its defense is not good. That gives Notre Dame a chance to keep building on what has been working. I want to see the run game continue to ascend, so keep riding Nolan James Jr. and Jonaz Walton . Quarterback CJ Carr can add a few more explosives through the air and play a little more consistently. The bigger thing I'll be watching is how Notre Dame starts each half. The Irish have gotten off to fast starts more consistently recently, and that needs to continue. Against Boston College, Notre Dame put up a 24-point second quarter, then opened the second half with an interception. Winning those middle eights and coming out of the locker room with some juice is another massive key. Notre Dame vs. SMU score prediction I expect SMU to score some points, but 17 feels like about the best the Mustangs can do without a sudden breakthrough in the run game. I think Notre Dame starts to take control somewhere in the second quarter and stays in command throughout the second half. Final score prediction: Notre Dame 41, SMU 17 That covers the spread and gives the Irish the decisive victory they need. If they handle business on Saturday, only Syracuse stands between Notre Dame and a playoff berth. away.headline: Notre Dame football could get one of its best defensive players back from injury for SMU game
away.blurb: SOUTH BEND, Ind. (WNDU) - One of Notre Dame’s top players on defense might return to the field for the first time since Week 1 when the Fighting Irish host SMU this upcoming Saturday. According to the team’s latest availability report, safety Brauntae Johnson has been upgraded from out to questionable. Several other Notre Dame starters on both sides of the ball are either out or questionable for Saturday’s game. Linebacker Drayk Bowen has been ruled out for the third consecutive game after suffering a right ankle injury against Navy . Cornerback DJ McKinney will miss his fourth consecutive game because of a right ankle injury suffered in Notre Dame’s loss to BYU . Starting defensive linemen Francis Brewu and Jason Onye are listed as questionable for the third consecutive week. Neither has played since being injured against Navy. Starting left tackle Will Black is also questionable after suffering a concussion Saturday against Boston College . Offensive linemen Charles Jagusah and Chris Terek are no longer listed on the injury report and will return to practice this week. Freeman said their return will be similar to Johnson’s, with the team evaluating how they respond in practice. Johnson, a preseason AP second-team All-American , has been sidelined since injuring his left foot in the season opener against Wisconsin . Head coach Marcus Freeman said Monday that he will be integrated back into practice to see how his body responds and whether he has an opportunity to play against SMU. away.headline: Notre Dame football regains two former starters for SMU week practice
away.blurb: SOUTH BEND — Brauntae Johnson, junior safety for Notre Dame football, was upgraded to questionable for Senior Night this week against Southern Methodist after missing nine full games due to left foot surgery. The Fort Wayne product, out since the first half of the season opener against Wisconsin, will return to practice on Tuesday and go from there. Johnson had hoped to make it back in time for the Miami game on Nov. 7, but his foot wasn’t close enough to 100% for that to happen. If it’s determined that he needs more practice time before facing an opponent, Johnson will be held out against the Mustangs and pointed toward the regular-season finale at Syracuse “This is the next phase of his progression in terms of return to play,” Freeman said. Left tackle Will Black is questionable with a concussion suffered after 27 offensive snaps against Boston College. Styles Prescod took over for the final 47 snaps without apparent issue. Defensive tackles Francis Brewu and Jason Onye remain questionable with knee injuries suffered in the first quarter against Navy on Halloween, but there’s finally some good news for hard-luck offensive lineman Charles Jagusah. Sixteen months after suffering a broken left humerus in a utility vehicle accident, the senior guard/tackle has been upgraded to questionable. Jagusah has undergone at least five surgical procedures as he deals with nerve damage in his upper arm, including a bone graft on March 18. “This is the next phase for him,” Freeman said. “That doesn’t mean he’ll go out there and start on Saturday, but that means he is actually practicing starting this week. That is huge. That’s amazing for that young man that has been through so much to be at the point now he can return to practice.” “He’s been training and rehabbing,” Irish coach Marcus Freeman said Monday Nov. 16. “We’re going to try to integrate him back into practice and see how his body responds. There are some football-specific movements that you do in practice that you can’t simulate in rehab.” Analysis: Play by play, Notre Dame football keeps it eyes on the prize Freeman noted the Rock Island, IL product has appeared in postseason games for the Irish, including the 2024 College Football Playoff semifinal and title games, but he’s yet to play a home game in college. “He’s never stepped on the field in a game at Notre Dame Stadium,” Freeman said. “If he can help us and we can find a role, how cool would that be to do that on Saturday? His journey has been amazing in terms of the things he’s overcome.” Senior offensive lineman Chris Terek, coming off right knee surgery in August, has been removed from the injury report as well. Mike Berardino covers Notre Dame football for the South Bend Tribune and NDInsider.com. Follow him on social media @MikeBerardino. There are some football-specific movements that you do in practice that you can’t simulate in rehab.” Analysis: Play by play, Notre Dame football keeps it eyes on the prize Freeman noted the Rock Island, IL product has appeared in postseason games for the Irish, including the 2024 College Football Playoff semifinal and title games, but he’s yet to play a home game in college. “He’s never stepped on the field in a game at Notre Dame Stadium,” Freeman said. “If he can help us and we can find a role, how cool would that be to do that on Saturday? His journey has been amazing in terms of the things he’s overcome.” Senior offensive lineman Chris Terek, coming off right knee surgery in August, has been removed from the injury report as well. picks.blurb: Missouri Defense Preview: Can Kentucky's offense bounce back? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games Texans cruise on TNF Ravens send Humphrey home 'GTA 6' impacts sports New Jersey Little Leaguer dies Kiffin's return to Tennessee Story by Wildcats Wire Missouri Defense Preview: Can Kentucky's offense bounce back? Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Thu, November 19, 2026 at 1:25 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels to CoMo for the final road game of the season against the Missouri Tigers. The Wildcats offense desperately needs to respond after scoring just 20 points in the last two weeks which has led to back-to-back losses. Missouri is a well coached, good all around football team and the defense has been consistent this season. However, the Tigers had their worst defensive performance of the season on the road last week against Georgia. Both teams are coming off back-to-back losses, Kentucky has scored just 20 points on offense in the past two weeks. Conversely, the Missouri defense has allowed 72 points over the last two weeks, albeit to Georgia and Texas. Kentucky has to find some of the offensive success they had before the bye week if they want to finish the season on a strong note. A win at Missouri would give the Wildcats six wins in SEC play, which has only happened once in program history and that was in the 1977 season. I fully expect a motivated performance from both teams to try and put an end to their respective two-game losing streaks. Kentucky's offensive line was named a semifinalist for the Joe Moore Award and have since had to of their worst performances of the season. Last week against Florida was the worst the offensive line has looked all season, so you can almost guarantee they will respond the right way in this game. Quiet frankly, they have to because if the offensive line plays like they did against the Gators they will be in danger of a winless month of November. Missouri's defense has playmakers at every level, but they will allow teams to move the football. Among SEC teams, the Tigers rank 10th in success rate allowed, 7th in pass success rate allowed and 12th in rush success rate allowed. Missouri also ranks 8th in the SEC in EPA/play allowed, 7th in EPA/pass allowed and 12th in EPA/rush allowed. The Tigers have also allowed explosive plays this season, as they rank 14th in the conference in explosive play rate allowed. This will be a difficult matchup for Kentucky, but it starts by winning the line of scrimmage and getting the run game going. The Wildcats averaged just two yards per carry against Florida and had just 61 rushing yards. They will lose this game if they can not turn that around, but the Missouri run defense has struggled at times this season. Kentucky has to stay ahead of the chains and that starts with the run game on early downs, which is something they had been good at all season. We mentioned the Tigers have playmakers at every level of the defense, and that starts up front with edge defender Daeden Hopkins. Hopkins leads the team in sacks (7) and tackles for loss (7.5). Linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez leads the middle of the defense, Rodriguez is a tackling machine with a team-leading 107 tackles on the season; he also has seven tackles for loss and 3.5 sacks on the year. The secondary is led by safety Santana Banner, Banner has 84 tackles on the season, 6 pass breakups and 2.5 tackles for loss. Kentucky has to account for these three players, as they are the strength of this Missouri defense at every level. Hopkins, Rodriguez and Banner have each forced two fumbles this season as well. They have consistently made big time plays for the Tigers all season long. Kentucky has to find ways to exploit this defense and avoid letting these three players make game changing plays. In a lot of ways, this matchup is about Kentucky after scoring just 20 points in the last eight quarters. The offense just is not playing well, and what happened on the line of scrimmage against Florida was alarming. Kentucky has to get the big blue wall back to playing like semifinalists for the Joe Moore Award. This offense lacks explosive plays and yards after contact ability, so they will continue to struggle if the offensive line can't get back to playing at a high level. Nine days ago, Kentucky Football was in the College Football Playoff conversation. Now, the Wildcats are trying to save a season that was turning into something special. The 21-14 loss to Florida on Saturday night at Kroger Field hurt more than most. Kentucky came in as a three-point favorite at home against a 5-4 Gators team. The Cats took a 7-2 lead into halftime and still led 14-13 going into the fourth quarter. Then Florida took over. Aaron Philo ran for 102 yards, the Gators ran for 211 as a team, and Kentucky managed just 61 rushing yards on 27 carries. That’s a season low for a team that came in averaging almost 164 per game. Will Stein didn’t sugarcoat it afterward. He said his team came up short in all three phases. That one stings because of how good this season had been. This was the team that went to College Station and beat No. 9 Texas A&M by 10. It came back from 17 down to win in overtime at South Carolina, beat No. 10 LSU 35-34 in overtime and sent the fans onto the field, then won in Norman. Kentucky was 7-1 and ranked in the top ten of the CFP rankings. Back-to-back losses to Tennessee and Florida later, the playoff dream is just about gone. But there’s still a lot to play for. Kentucky is 7-3 and bowl eligible with two games left: at Missouri and Louisville at home. Win both, then win a bowl game, and Kentucky reaches 10 wins. The program has only done that four times in its history: 1950, 1977, 2018 and 2021. In Stein’s first year, against what his own players called a whole lot of doubt back in August, that would be a remarkable finish. It starts Saturday night in Columbia. Matchup: Kentucky (7-3) at Missouri (6-4, 3-4 SEC) When: Saturday, Nov. 21, 7:30 p.m. ET Where: Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium, Columbia, MO. TV: SEC Network Odds: Missouri -6.5, over/under 50.5 (FanDuel) All-time series: Kentucky leads 9-5 Last meeting: Missouri won 38-21 in Lexington in 2023 Opponent at a Glance: Missouri Tigers Head coach: Eli Drinkwitz (7th season) Missouri started the year ranked No. 25 in the preseason polls. For a while, it looked like the Tigers were exactly who people thought they were. They blew out Florida 45-17, held Texas A&M to six points in a 27-6 win and beat Arkansas by 24. The problem is what happened against good teams. Missouri lost at Mississippi State in September, lost 31-3 at Ole Miss, lost 34-20 at home to Texas and just got rolled 48-21 by No. 1 Georgia in Athens. Two straight losses ended the Tigers’ playoff hopes. The Georgia game was ugly from the first snap. Quarterback Austin Simmons threw an interception on the first play, Georgia scored two plays later, and Missouri was down 31 at halftime. Drinkwitz called it “not a good plan offensively or defensively,” and the Tigers went 2-for-11 on third down. Missouri 2026 Results W 54-14 vs. Arkansas-Pine Bluff W 38-21 vs. Kansas W 27-17 vs. Troy L 31-24 at Mississippi State W 45-17 vs. Florida W 27-6 vs. Texas A&M L 31-3 at Ole Miss W 34-10 at Arkansas L 34-20 vs. Texas L 48-21 at Georgia Players to Know QB Austin Simmons: He won the job over Matt Zollers in the spring and opened the season 17 of 19 for 252 yards and four touchdowns. When he gets protection he can pick you apart. RB Ahmad Hardy: A preseason AP First Team All-American and the engine of the run game. Kentucky’s run defense has to be better than it was against Florida. RB Jamal Roberts: The second back in a deep backfield. WR Donovan Olugbode: Simmons’ favorite target and the guy they go to on third down. OL Cayden Green: A preseason Second Team All-American who anchors the line. Keys to the Game Fix the run defense. Florida ran 48 times for 211 yards and wore Kentucky down in the second half. Missouri will try the exact same thing with Hardy. If Kentucky can’t set the edge, it’s going to be a long night. Get the run game going again. Kentucky’s offense works when the run sets up Kenny Minchey. Sixty-one rushing yards won’t win in the SEC, let alone on the road at night. Attack the secondary. Pass defense has been Missouri’s weak spot all year. Georgia’s Gunner Stockton went 18 of 24 for 252 yards. Minchey needs to take his shots. Start fast. Missouri has started slow on the road and on the ropes. Kentucky has led into the second half against Alabama, Tennessee, and Florida and lost all three. The second half is where this team has to grow up. Win the turnover battle. Kentucky’s big wins this year came down to a play here and there. Simmons has been careless with the ball against good defenses. Make him pay. Our Early Prediction This one comes down to which team handles adversity better. Both are coming off back-to-back losses, and both had playoff hopes that are now gone. Missouri has the home field and is favored by almost a touchdown. Kentucky has the head coach who has won close games all year. What gives me some hope is the bounce back. After Alabama blew them out, the Cats went on the road and beat Texas A&M. Stein has had a whole week to get this team’s attention after being called out for not looking like themselves. I think Kentucky responds. It won’t be pretty, but the Cats grind out a road win and stay alive for a 10-win season. Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. picks.headline: How No. 16 Kentucky football and Missouri match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Kentucky’s Kenny Minchey (68.8% completions, 2,160 yards, 15 touchdowns vs. two interceptions) had a challenging game in UK’s 21-14 upset loss to visiting Florida last week. The 6-foot-2, 211-pound product of Hendersonville, Tennessee, completed only 15 of 26 passes for 181 yards with one touchdown. In going 0-2 since returning from an Oct. 31 open week, Kentucky has allowed too much pressure on its QB. Minchey has been sacked six times and hurried 10 times total in losses to Tennessee and Florida. • Missouri’s Austin Simmons (62.3% completions, 2,379 yards, 21 touchdowns vs. three interceptions) has thrown for seven combined touchdowns in Mizzou’s past three games. A 6-4, 220-pound product of Miami, Simmons has already started a game vs. UK. Playing last season for Ole Miss, Simmons made his first career road start at Kroger Field. The QB threw two early picks as Ole Miss fell behind 10-0. Simmons steadied, however, and threw for 235 yards and ran for 44 yards and a TD as the Rebels rallied to beat Kentucky 30-23. Advantage : Missouri Running backs • UK leading rusher CJ Baxter (562 yards, 5.3 yards a carry, eight touchdowns; 13 catches, 91 yards, one TD) caught a 5-yard touchdown pass in the loss vs. Florida but had a hard time on the ground vs. the Gators. The 6-1, 230-pound product of Boynton Beach, Florida, rushed 8 times for 21 yards vs. his home-state school. Since missing the Oklahoma game due to injury, Baxter has subsequently carried 20 times for 78 yards in the three games. Third-year player Jason Patterson (495 yards, 6 yards a carry, three TDs) had 22 yards on five rushes vs. Florida and caught a pass for nine yards. • Missouri’s Jamal Roberts (1,133 yards, 5 yards a carry, nine touchdowns) is second in the SEC in rushing. A 6-foot, 216-pound St. Louis product, Roberts has run for 100 yards or more in five games this season, and has gone above 200 yards rushing in a game twice. Ahmad Hardy led the SEC in rushing in 2025, running for 1,649 yards and 16 touchdowns. However, the 5-10, 210-pound product of Oma, Mississippi, missed the first seven games this season as he recovered from being shot in the left leg May 10 while attending an outdoor concert in Laurel, Mississippi. Since returning three games ago, Hardy has carried 10 times for 41 yards. Wide receivers • Kentucky freshman Kenny Darby (49 catches, 601 yards, three touchdowns) needs two catches and 29 receiving yards to shatter Barion Brown’s UK freshman marks (50 receptions, 628 receiving yards in 2022) for most catches and receiving yards in a season. Second-year player DJ Miller (26, 324, 1) caught four passes for 80 yards vs. Florida but also had a costly drop on UK’s final offensive possession of the game. • Missouri’s Cayden Lee is second in the SEC in receptions and first in the conference in receiving yards (879). A transfer from Ole Miss, the 5-11, 180-pound fourth-year player has caught at least five passes in every Mizzou game in 2026 other than last week’s 48-21 loss at No. 1 Georgia, when he was held to three receptions for 44 yards. Lee caught one pass for eight yards for Ole Miss in its win at Kentucky last season. Sophomore Donovan Olugbode is also having a big year for Missouri. The 6-2, 210-pound Chicago product has made 47 catches for 691 yards and eight touchdowns. • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez is tied for fifth in the FBS in receptions by a tight end with 50. The 6-4, 249-pound, third-year player from Covington Catholic High School has turned those team-high 50 receptions into 467 receiving yards and three touchdowns. A model of consistency, Rodriguez has caught either five or six passes in each of UK’s past six games. • Missouri’s Brett Norfleet has 14 catches for 120 yards and two TDs. The 6-6, 255-pound fourth-year player caught one pass for seven yards in last week’s loss to Georgia. Jude James has averaged 10 yards a catch on his seven receptions. Advantage : Kentucky Offensive line • In the losses to Tennessee and Florida the past two weeks, Kentucky right tackle Malachi Wood has seemed to struggle in pass protection. Of the 6-8, 329-pound Madison Central product, Will Stein said “We all know, I know, (I) think everybody on our team knows (Wood’s) talent level is as good as you’re going to find in the country. It’s just consistency at that position.” • Missouri left tackle Cayden Green is the pillar of a Tigers offensive front that has surrendered the fewest QB sacks (nine) in the SEC. After starting five times for Oklahoma in 2023, Green transferred to Mizzou and started all 13 games in 2024 at left guard. Since switching to left tackle prior to the 2025 season, the 6-5, 324-pound Green has become a standout. So far in 2026, he has not allowed a sack or quarterback hit. Defensive line • Kentucky end Mi’Quise Humphrey-Grace (36 tackles, six sacks, nine tackles for loss, nine quarterback hurries) had a streak of three straight games with at least one sack snapped vs. Florida. Tackle Tavion Gadson (33 tackles, three sacks, five TFL, two pass breakups, two fumble recoveries) also made four stops against the Gators. Gadson has now gone three games without a sack. • Missouri defensive end Daeden Hopkins is fourth in the SEC with seven sacks. The 6-6, 250-pound second-year player has also been credited with 11 quarterback hurries. A transfer from Miami, second-year tackle Donta Simpson has emerged as a disruptor for Eli Drinkwitz and Co. The 6-4, 300-pound Simpson has six QB sacks, 7.5 tackles for loss and eight QB hurries. Advantage : Even • Even though Kentucky MLB Grant Godfrey (13 tackles) and WLB Bo Barnes (nine stops) were UK’s two leading tacklers vs. Florida, the prevailing thought was that UF’s ample success with the QB run game owed, in some part, to the Wildcats’ linebackers not fitting the run properly. “There were some big, big missed tackles in the game that sprung explosive runs by their quarterback,” Will Stein said. “That goes back to us not executing the fundamentals and technique of our position.” • Missouri WLB Nicholas Rodriguez leads the SEC in tackles with 107. The 6-foot, 225-pound Miami product has made at least 11 tackles in eight of Mizzou’s 10 games to date. MLB Robert Woodyard Jr ., a transfer from Auburn, is 22nd in the SEC with 64 tackles and has forced two fumbles and picked off a pass. Defensive backs • Kentucky safeties Jordan Castell and Ty Bryant are tied for second in the SEC in interceptions with four apiece. However, neither has a pick in either of UK’s past two games, the losses at Tennessee and to Florida. Castell, a 6-2, 211-pound product of Orlando, is ninth in the SEC with 76 tackles. Bryant, a 6-foot, 196-pound Lexington native, is 12th in the SEC with 74 stops. • Missouri cornerbacks Sione Laulea and Chris Graves Jr. are tied for second in the SEC with 10 passes successfully defended. Strong safety Santana Banner has recovered two fumbles and broken up six passes. Special teams • Kentucky place-kicker Adam Zouagui is 12 of 15 on field-goal tries with a long make of 52 yards. For the second time this season, UK switched punters vs. Florida. After Wilson Berry punted for four games (averaging 42.6 yards a kick), UK went back to its original starting punter of 2026, Murray State transfer Thomas O’Hara , vs. the Gators. O’Hara kicked three times vs. UF and averaged 46.3 yards a kick. On the season, O’Hara, an Australian, has averaged 41.5 yards on 20 punts. • Missouri place-kicker Blake Craig has missed nine of his 24 field-goal tries this season but has a long make of 53 yards. Craig has been better from outside 50 yards (5 of 7, 71.4%) than from inside 50 yards (10 of 17, 58.8%). Punter Brunno Reus is averaging 44.47 yards a kick and has stopped 18 of 47 punts inside the opponent’s 20-yard line. Punt returner DaMarion Fowlkes averaged 10 yards a return and had a 68-yard TD vs. Troy. As a kickoff returner, Fowlkes is averaging 24.8 yards on 12 returns. away.blurb: Even if Kentucky does return to the playoff hunt, beating Missouri would be big for the program. Backup linebacker Alex Afari was an unexpected addition to the “out” list on Wednesday’s SEC availability report. Nickel back Jaden Smith (ACL) is out for the season. Backup linebacker Antwan Smith (ankle) might be back for the bowl game but is not expected to return in the regular season. Linebacker Quintavion Norman, who primarily contributes on special teams, is also out this week. Cornerback Grant Grayton, who has missed the past eight games with an injury, is listed as doubtful. Even if he does not play this week, that is a sign he is nearing a return. Wide receiver Nic Anderson, who has missed two of the past three games, was listed as questionable. Like Kentucky, Missouri has lost its past two games, but the Tigers scored more points in losses to Texas and Georgia than the Wildcats did in losses to Tennessee and Florida. The model projects that chance would jump to 20% with a win in Columbia. Even if Kentucky wins its final two games, it still needs help in the form of losses from at least four of BYU, Wake Forest, Texas Tech, Oregon, Ohio State and Iowa. All Kentucky can control is its own performance, though. Kentucky has only won six SEC games in a season once previously (1977). It has not won four road games in a season since 1984. It has not won four SEC road games since 1977. Finishing at 6-3 in SEC play would give Kentucky a leg up in the pecking order for the Citrus Bowl, which has the first pick of SEC teams after the playoff is filled. A Citrus Bowl appearance versus a traditional Big Ten power would be a nice consolation prize for missing the playoff. The Tigers, who have dropped their last two games and fallen out of College Football Playoff contention, will host Kentucky on Saturday at 7:30 p.m ET. Mizzou sophomore defensive tackle Donta Simpson Jr. has re-signed with the Tigers for the 2027 season, On3 and Rivals transfer portal reporter Hayes Fawcett reported Thursday night. The 6-foot-4, 300-pound defensive lineman transferred to Missouri after spending his freshman season at Miami. He appeared in eight games for the Hurricanes in 2025, recording four tackles and 1.5 tackles for loss without managing a sack. Simpson has made considerable progress since joining the Tigers. Despite missing more than a month during the offseason because of an illness that also delayed his participation in fall camp, he has emerged as one of Missouri’s most productive defensive players. I know rivalry games can make records look meaningless, and the Golden Bears would love nothing more than to keep their neighbors out of a bowl game. But at some point, I have to back the team that's actually moving in the right direction. Stanford has won three of its last four, while Cal has lost four straight and looks completely out of answers under Tosh Lupoi. The Cardinal can become bowl eligible for the first time since 2018, and I think they're playing with the urgency to make that happen. What's changed for Stanford is that the offense finally has something it can lean on. Micah Ford has rushed for at least 145 yards in three of the last four games, and he's averaging 137.5 rushing yards since the win over Elon. He just ran for 149 yards and three touchdowns in a 40-22 victory at Virginia Tech. That's a big deal against a Cal defense allowing 186.2 rushing yards per game. Stanford hasn't been a great rushing team over the entire season, but Ford's recent form gives the Cardinal a way to control possessions instead of asking Davis Warren to do everything. Warren has quietly done a nice job protecting the football. He's thrown for 2,406 yards with 14 touchdowns and only three interceptions, despite ranking among the national leaders in pass attempts. Stanford is still converting just 31.7 percent of its third downs, so it's not as though every offensive problem has disappeared. But when you can get the running game going and avoid handing the opponent short fields, you give yourself a much better chance to win close games. That's been missing from this program for a while. Cal's offense is the bigger concern for me. The Bears are scoring just 20.4 points per game and averaging only 78.7 rushing yards. That's an awful lot of pressure on Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele, who's thrown 11 touchdowns against eight interceptions. Chase Hendricks has been productive with 65 catches, but defenses don't have to respect the run nearly enough. Cal managed seven points at Virginia last week, and that loss followed defeats to Wake Forest, SMU and NC State. Those four losses have come by at least three touchdowns apiece. That's not a team that's simply catching a few unlucky breaks. I won't pretend Stanford is some defensive powerhouse. The Cardinal allow 35.8 points and nearly 449 yards per game, numbers that give Cal a legitimate opportunity to move the ball. But Stanford forced three turnovers against Virginia Tech, with Charlie Eckhardt recording two interceptions and a forced fumble. That was the Cardinal's first road win since 2024, snapping a 15-game skid away from home. The defense doesn't suddenly become great because of one afternoon, but there are signs of improvement when the offense gives it a chance. The travel angle is another reason I don't mind the road favorite here. Stanford has been crushed on several cross-country trips since joining the ACC, but going from Palo Alto to Berkeley is hardly the same situation. Cal also returns home after three straight road games, so maybe getting back to its own building helps. They haven't played in Berkeley since October 17, so there's some uncertainty there. The Bears have won the last two Big Games played in Berkeley, and that matters in a rivalry. Stanford, though, took back the Axe with a 31-10 win last season. Now there's a bowl bid waiting on the other side of another rivalry victory, while Cal is already eliminated from postseason consideration. away.headline: Cal-Stanford injury report: Several key Bears players questionable
away.blurb: Although there are no new Cal players listed as being out, four starters are listed as questionable. Starting wide receiver Ian Strong, who missed last week's game, as well as defensive back Daniel Harris, safety Isaiah Crosby and inside linebacker JD McKinley are the four Cal starters listed as questionable. Safety Aiden Manutai, outside linebacker Justin Beadles and defensive lineman Ashun Shepphard are also Cal players expected to get playing time if they are healthy, but all three are listed as questionable. Also of interest is the fact that quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele and running back Adam Mohammed are listed as probable. That indicates they are likely to play against Stanford, but it also suggests they are nursing some injuries. Three Cal players listed as being out for the Big Game are the same players who have been sidelined for virtually the entire season -- running back Carter Vargas, defensive lineman Nate Burrell and tight end Dorian Thomas. This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/cal as Cal-Stanford Injury Report: Several Key Bears Players Questionable . The initial injury report for Saturday's Cal-Stanford game was released Wednesday night, and a number of key Cal players are listed. Strong is the Bears' second-leading receiver with 35 catches for 478 yards, while McKinley, who also missed last week's game, is the team's co-leader in sacks with three. Crosby is second on the team in tackles with 56 and he also has an interception and two tackles for loss. Harris is fifth on the team in tackles with 37, and he also has three tackles for loss and four quarterback hurries. Cal is 3-7 overall and is riding a four-game losing streak. The Bears will host Stanford (5-5, 4-5 ACC) in Saturday's Big Game starting at 4:30 p.m. The Cardinal would become bowl-eligible if it beats Cal. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth TCU (5–5, 3–4 Big 12), Utah (10–0, 7–0) TCU defeated Utah on the road in 2024, 13-7 What's at stake? The TCU Horned Frogs will face one of their toughest challenges of the season Saturday when they host No. 2 Utah at Amon G. Carter Stadium. The Frogs are coming off a 20-10 victory over Kansas State , while the Utes enter the matchup looking to keep their undefeated season alive. Utah is 10-0 overall and 7-0 in Big 12 play. Saturday's matchup will mark the highest-ranked opponent to visit Amon G. Carter Stadium since No. 2 Texas in 1970. It also marks TCU's final home game of the season before the Frogs travel to face Texas Tech on Thanksgiving Day. With a win, TCU would secure bowl eligibility and pull off one of the biggest upsets of the college football season. When TCU has the ball Quarterback Jaden Craig will be a key factor in TCU's ability to keep up with Utah's offense. Craig has thrown for 2,664 yards, 13 touchdowns and seven interceptions this season. He is coming off a 225-yard performance against Kansas State, where he also threw a touchdown pass. The Horned Frogs will need to find ways to create offensive opportunities without relying entirely on Craig's arm. Establishing the run game and finding success on early downs will be important against a Utah defense that has helped the Utes remain undefeated. Craig has also been dealing with an ankle injury that has limited his mobility. However, head coach Sonny Dykes said during Tuesday's midweek news conference that Craig is showing improvement and is expected to play Saturday. "I would expect him to play. He was a lot better today than he was yesterday. I would anticipate him being able to practice tomorrow and play on Saturday," Dykes said Tuesday. TCU will need to sustain drives, limit mistakes and take advantage of its scoring opportunities if it hopes to pull off the upset. The Frogs showed they can do that with their 20-10 victory over Kansas State. When Kansas State has the ball Undefeated Utah has been one of the strongest teams in the Big 12 this season and is looking to secure a spot in the conference championship game. The Utes will be one of TCU's toughest defensive challenges yet. The Frogs will need to limit Utah's scoring opportunities and find ways to slow down its offense if they hope to keep the game competitive. Quarterback Devon Dampier has completed 66.5% of his passes for 2,257 yards, 22 touchdowns and eight interceptions this season. His ability to make plays through the air will put pressure on TCU's secondary. TCU's defense will need to create pressure, limit big plays and force Utah into difficult third-down situations. If the Frogs cannot slow down Dampier and the Utes' offense, it could be a long night for the defense. This will be one of the toughest games of the season for the Horned Frogs. TCU is coming off a big win over Kansas State and will be hungry to prove it can compete with one of the best teams in the country. While I expect the Frogs to put up a fight, they have struggled to perform consistently under pressure this season. Utah has remained undefeated for a reason, and its strength on both sides of the ball will make this a difficult matchup for TCU. I expect the Horned Frogs to compete early, but Utah's consistency will ultimately be too much to overcome. Utah's special teams made huge strides in the team's 40-39 win over Arizona. Kicker Dillon Curtis was 2-for-2 on field goals — including a 53-yard make — and 4-for-4 on extra points, including the go-ahead PAT in the fourth quarter. But a muffed punt by Mana Carvalho in the fourth quarter brought down the overall grade for special teams. Carvalho has had a number of close calls this season, and one finally went the wrong way for him against the Wildcats. The Utes, up by five, had just forced an Arizona punt with 10:27 left and were in position to possibly take a two-score lead with a successful offensive drive. Carvalho should have either fair caught the punt or let it go with Dwight Bootle II barreling down on him, but Carvalho tried to field it and muffed it, then got rocked by Bootle and had to be helped off the field and into the medical tent. Utah's defense held strong as Arizona threatened in the red zone on the ensuing drive, forcing a field goal. Those saved four points would prove crucial in a one-point win.
